description: **Oqtane Marketplace order ingestion, license and trial lifecycle, with customer communications.**
releaseNotes:
## v1.2.0

The manual order form can start from the catalogue. An optional product and licence-option picker - built from the Products tab - fills the product name, licence name, type, amount and expiry once. Every field stays editable, Free entry remains the default, and the stored order is still a manual backfill with no package id. No migration runs; existing data and the 1.1.0 catalogue are unchanged. Requires StudioElf CRM 1.8.0 or later.

## v1.1.0

The first release after 1.0.0 bundles the product and licence catalogue with a selectable Marketplace import, the transaction currency, the stored reporting-currency value, and user-default paging. Migration `01010000_Release110` creates the catalogue tables and adds the order currency column; `01010100_OrderBaseCurrency` adds the reporting columns; `01010200_OptionNamePerProduct` makes an option name unique per product instead of per module; `01010300_ProductMarketplaceMetadata` adds the product type, version, release date and logo columns.

**Product and licence catalogue.** Products and their licence options are managed on the settings screen - a product links on its marketplace package id, each option's name is the license name the marketplace sends and is unique within that product. Two products may sell the same option name; an order resolves its option within the product its package id matched, while a hand-entered order resolves a shared name only when one product defines it. The catalogue names products in the UI, emails and events, classifies trial versus purchase from the matched option's scope, and computes each order's expiry from the option's own term (day, month or year counted from the purchase date). Known products appear automatically; products seen on real orders are discovered for naming. Each product also shows its Marketplace type (Module or Theme), version, release date and logo, with a type badge in the one list both types share. Import from Marketplace reads the same registry JSON as Manage Modules and Manage Themes and shows a selection list filtered by a configurable prefix, saving only the ticked products: new ones start ticked, and an existing one can be updated to fill a blank display name and blank metadata or replace its description, type, version, release date and logo while its non-blank name, renewal lead time and options are kept. Select all, Clear selection and Toggle selection buttons in the panel header select every applicable row, clear them, or invert each one, and a row that cannot be applied stays disabled. A positive Marketplace trial period automatically adds or corrects one Trial License option (type Trial, term that many days) so a trial order is classified and dated without hand entry. The catalogue's pager offers 5, 10, 15, 20 or All for the current visit, a Product type filter narrows the list to All types, Modules or Themes, every card carries a Module, Theme or Not specified badge, and the page is kept while a product is edited or the size changes. Per-product trial lengths come from the product's own Trial option. A product's renewal-notice lead time plans a transactional subscription renewal reminder, with the listed fee and charge date, before expiry; new products start at 14 days.

**Transaction currency.** The marketplace bills in USD and its payload carries no currency, so each order stores the currency beside its amount; existing rows are backfilled with USD. Amounts display as `USD 30.00` in the order list, the catalogue's fee column, the manual order form and the renewal email's `{{Fee}}` token. The transaction record is never converted.

**Stored reporting value.** Each positive-amount order captures the CRM's reporting-currency conversion once, after the order is committed, and stores it: the reporting amount, the applied rate and its effective date, or the fixed `SameCurrency`, `NoRate` or `Unconfigured` outcome. Existing orders are backfilled by the nightly lifecycle scan at each order's own date. The expanded order detail reads the stored snapshot only, so a page load makes no CRM call and a later rate change cannot rewrite history. A manager can edit the stored amount to the actual value converted; that sets `Manual`, clears the automatic rate and never touches the transaction amount or currency.

**Paging.** Order, trial and communication lists page at the CRM user's saved default page size (falling back to the CRM module default, then 20), with no second size picker. Communications now pages and resets to page 1 when a filter changes. The Products catalogue keeps its current page while a product is edited or the page size changes.

**Fixes.** The scheduled jobs now walk each tenant's sites and then each site's modules, setting the site alias before any site-bound work, instead of iterating a flat module-id list. Marketplace orders are now actually saved - the webhook previously built the order but never added it to the context. A minimal contact is created with an explicit empty `LastName`. Product catalogue writes carry the site antiforgery token, so a save or import no longer answers a bare 400. Option names are unique per product through migration `01010200_OptionNamePerProduct`. List responses are public top-level DTOs, so .NET Reactor can no longer leave the Products tab and the order and communication lists and counts empty under the protected build. The Products pager passes `CurrentPage` and `OnPageChange`, so editing a product or changing the page size no longer returns to page 1. Marketplace import reads theme packages as well as modules, so a product sold as a theme is selectable. A database that already recorded 1.1.0 from a pre-release build runs `Upgrade-1.1.0-OptionNamePerProduct.sql` once if that fix was never applied, then `Upgrade-1.1.0-ProductMetadata.sql`; both ship in the package and both are idempotent. Requires StudioElf CRM 1.8.0 or later.

## v1.0.0

First release. Marketplace order ingestion over a secret-authenticated webhook, trial and purchase lifecycle state on UTC boundaries, contact resolution by email with optional AI Capture, masked license keys with a manager-only reveal, and two outbound CRM webhook events (`license.order_received`, `license.trial_started`).

The 1.0.0 package required Oqtane 10.2.6 and StudioElf CRM 1.6.0. Migrations ran automatically on the first start after install.
summary: Ingest Oqtane Marketplace orders over one secret-authenticated webhook, resolve them against a product and licence catalogue managed on screen or through a selectable Marketplace import that keeps module and theme metadata and brings a Marketplace trial's Trial License option with it, track licence and trial lifecycle against UTC boundaries, match buyers to CRM contacts, and keep licence keys masked behind a manager-only reveal. A manual backfill can start from the catalogue or be typed freely. Built for Oqtane 10.2.6 and StudioElf CRM 1.8.0.
